messages:
support: FYI — AcmeCorp just opened a Sev2. Their p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms around 2024-07-28 14:05 UTC. They've attached a dashboard and a few traces: https://app.redwood/d/acme/p99-dashboard — customer is blocking a release.

ingrid: ack. can you paste the affected endpoint + sample request? also any auth failures or errors?

support: POST /v1/generate (model: rwkv-3b-v1 by default), prompt length ~1000 tokens, concurrency ~= 4. No 5xxs reported, just tails. Attaching one trace link: https://traces.redwood/acme/trace/0abc

jamal: I pulled the dashboard. The p99 panel is a rollup from histo-buckets, looks like we rebinned buckets yesterday; panel uses old bucket boundaries. raw histogram traces still show most requests under 200ms.

kevin: can you paste the dashboard query? I want to compare the rollup vs raw percentile.

jamal: sure — panel uses this rollup query: ```SELECT rollup_quantile(hist_latency, 0.99, bucket_size=50) FROM requests WHERE service='inference' AND model='rwkv-3b-v1' GROUP BY 1m``` The raw percentile widget uses streaming quantiles from traces. The rollup quantile impl does interpolation over discrete buckets; when bucket boundaries changed it can skew p99 upward.

nina: customer also shared a quick repro: repeating the same request with concurrency 4 produces tail spikes on their side. They asked for a short-term mitigation while we dig.

ops-bot: autoscaler: increased pool "inference-prod-rwkv-3b" from 8 -> 12 nodes at 2024-07-28T14:08:20Z due to latency SLO breach.

ingrid: two action items: 1) confirm whether this is a dashboard/reporting artifact vs real tail regression; 2) if real, provide short-term customer mitigation. jamal — can you run a raw quantile query over traces for the last 30m?

jamal: running now. raw traces 14:00-14:20 show p99 ~160ms, p95 ~110ms. So the service tail didn't change much. The rollup panel spikes to ~900ms because buckets shifted from 10ms increments to 50ms increments at 14:03 during a metrics ingest config update.

kevin: great catch. that explains the mismatch. we should revert the rollup panel to use the new bucket mapping or re-run an aggregation that maps old buckets to new boundaries. For immediate customer confidence: we can share the raw trace p99 and offer route their traffic to dedicated capacity for a few hours.

nina: customer wants something visible now. I'll post a quick note with the raw p99 numbers and that we're investigating metric/visualization mismatch. they accepted temporary routing to dedicated if ops can do it.

ingrid: ops, can we provision a dedicated route for acme (customer id: acme-42) and set a fallback to rwkv-3b-quantized variant? low risk.

ops-bot: routing: created temporary route acme-42 -> dedicated-pool-7, effective 14:12 UTC.

jamal: follow-up: file a postmortem on the metrics-ingest config change that altered bucketization without updating rollup queries. Recommend: 1) add a changelog/alert when bucket schema changes, 2) add test to dashboard pipeline that compares rollup vs raw-percentile on a sample workload.

kevin: also add a helper on dashboards that surfaces which bucket schema a panel expects. small UI hint would reduce confusion.

support: communicated to customer with raw numbers + temporary dedicated routing. customer acknowledged, will monitor. Ticket #INC-2024-089 created.

ingrid: closing loop here. if no further regression shows up after the routing, mark this as metrics-display incident and not a runtime regression. I'll own the follow-up with observability.

nina: thanks team. I'll send the customer the acceptance note and link to INC-2024-089.

jamal: one more: we should consider backfilling the rollup aggregation for the 14:00-14:10 window so historical dashboards read correctly. adding to the incident ticket.

kevin: noted. good catch all :thumbsup:
